title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 provisional railway-clock table
scope: Backend-only structured clock controls for the Arizona-to-San-Diego sequence, 22-26 April 1892. The table separates contemporaneous correspondence from exact-year and near-contemporary timetable controls and from constrained inference.
frontend_policy: Backend only. Do not publish this table, sketchbook image associations, daylight eliminations or inferred railway minutes on public Pages without a separate explicit sync decision.

evidence_grades.A: Contemporaneous primary correspondence/postcard explicitly reporting place/date/time or immediate travel sequence.
evidence_grades.A-: Same-year timetable very close to target date, or high-confidence inference tightly bounded by multiple A-grade facts.
evidence_grades.B: Near-contemporary timetable/service table demonstrating a stable clock pattern but not exact for the target date.
evidence_grades.C: Later structural/route analogue; useful only for persistent geometry or service pattern.

clock_guard: Historical railroad times are retained as printed/reported clock readings. Do not silently convert them to modern UTC offsets. Where a timetable labels a time standard, preserve that label. Daylight analysis should first compare local solar conditions with the historical clock sequence and state all assumptions.

rows.finding: Wagon excursion a few miles into mountains/desert; plan to finish Tempe next day, spend the night at Maricopa, then take the Sunday-morning California train.
Transfer to the Southern Pacific junction and overnight at Maricopa is required by Rudolf's forward plan and next-day presence.

rows.exactness: same-year close control; not issue-specific proof for 24 April
rows.finding: Southern Pacific westbound passes Maricopa at about 6:35 A.M.; later 1892 issues repeat the same time.
rows.interpretation: Strong contextual fit with Rudolf's Sunday-morning California departure and 24 April Maricopa sketches/cards.
rows.guard: Do not write 'Rudolf's train departed 6:35' until an April 24/April issue table is recovered.

rows.finding: Two filmed landscapes are captioned Maricopa, 24 April 1892; current interpretation is station-adjacent / transit observation rather than a separate collecting excursion.
rows.guard: The drawings do not prove they were executed aboard the moving train.

rows.source_class: Arizona Sentinel reproduction of Southern Pacific Pacific System timetable
rows.exactness: near-contemporary stable-service control, not exact 1892 proof
rows.finding: Westbound row gives Yuma departure about 12:40 P.M. toward Banning, Colton, Los Angeles and onward points.
rows.interpretation: Together with the Maricopa 6:35 close control and Rudolf's Los Angeles overnight, this produces a coherent provisional clock skeleton.
rows.guard: The printed table predates Rudolf's trip and must be replaced by an 1892 issue if recovered.

rows.station_or_segment: Maricopa → Yuma → California desert → Salton depression → San Jacinto approach
rows.exactness: exact preceding day and ordered ecological/landscape sequence; internal minutes unresolved
rows.finding: Rudolf explicitly narrates the preceding day's progression through Arizona/Yuma cactus landscape, California near-barren desert, the Salton depression, then a climb past snow-covered San Jacinto with changing Yucca/Opuntia/Abronia vegetation.
rows.sketchbook_relation: Rakow pp. 12-13 now belong to this 24 April corridor with high confidence, while exact massif/milepoint remains unresolved.

rows.finding: Rudolf says they reached Los Angeles 'at 10', had to stay overnight, and the San Diego train left next morning at 8:45. Combined with 25 April 13:00 San Diego arrival, 10 p.m. is overwhelmingly more plausible than 10 a.m.
rows.guard: Display as ca. 22:00 / high-confidence inference, not a verbatim PM notation.

rows.finding: Morning departure toward San Diego at 8:45.
Rudolf reports first reaching/seeing the Pacific around 10 in the morning, after which the ocean remained in view toward San Diego.
rows.guard: Needs an April/May 1892 Southern California Railway/Santa Fe station table to locate the first-ocean-view window.

rows.finding: Rudolf explicitly says he arrived at 1 p.m.; the 26 April letter independently confirms the party had already been in San Diego the previous afternoon.
